question: We have identical panels in several different plant locations and have no issues whatsoever. At this particular site we have three panels located very close to one another on a mezzanine. On about a dozen drives in two of the panels we get nuisance faults at seemingly random time intervals (Phase UV Short, Phase UW Short, Phase VW Short). All cabling is belden shielded VFD cable with the shield terminated at the drive as well as the motor.  We have tried shielding the motor connections from the drive to the Terminal blocks where field connections are made. This did not help. We recently installed grounding rods at the panel location. This did not help.  All drives have earth ground connected to the backplane (which is in turn tied into the grounding rod and main supply neutral). All VFD cable lengths are short enough to not require line reactors or the like.  We have pulled the motor leads off of a drive and had that drive trip with no load attached (hardware overcurrent on the output terminals). We have swapped a new drive with the one that tripped with no load attached and still had it fault. May be unrelated - There is a lot of process control nearby (pumps, etc). The temperature reading on the a/c for both problem panelsl jumps all over the place. But, one if the a/c units shipped DOA so this may be non-related. All panels are fed off the same PDP yet we are only getting the nuisance faults in two of the three panels. There are 40+ drives in one problem panel and nearly 30 in the other problem panel. The non-problem panel has 27 drives. Some drives trip 7-8 times more often than the others. The ones that fault the most are all mounted closely to some piece of ancillary equipment that has its own separate power feed. (may be unrelated) No faults occur on any of the VFDs that are mounted on the mezzanine (grounded steel structure) in which the panels are located.  Faults only occur on conveyor sections that are mounted along a cement floor.  Faults do not seem to be temperature related as the panels are always cool feeling.  I have trended the input voltage to a problem drive and the voltage at the input (Fluke 289) never dipped below 469vac while the highest spike was somewhere around 481vac.  Changing the carrier frequency did not help. Using software current limits in the drive did not help. Voltage at the drive output compared to voltage at the motor peckerhead is within 1% between all three phases of the drive that faults most often. resistance between phases of the drive that faults most often is within 1%. We have swapped a known bad motor with a known good one. This did not help. We have ran a shielded cable outside the cable tray directly to the closest problem motor (less than 50ft). This did not help. Any input or troubleshooting suggestions would be greatly appreciated. I have contacted Rockwell half a dozen times and the techs are always clueless.
search_note: Searched the fault table for 'Phase UV Short'/'Phase UW Short' (p74) — the manual lists only generic causes (shorted motor/wiring) and the standard remedy (check wiring, replace drive). It does not address intermittent multi-drive EMI/grounding/interference across adjacent panels with no load fault reproduction — that is a field electrical-interference investigation beyond the fault table's scope.
